wolfram.note: compute-engine's ToString prints a list in our own notatio/Epsil source syntax ([1, 2, 3]), by design; Wolfram prints its own native list syntax ({1, 2, 3}).
Wolfram's ToString uses OutputForm, a 2-D text layout (" 2\nx"); ours writes InputForm on one line.
Wolfram's default term order for Plus prints the integer first ("1 + x"); ours prints the variable first ("x + 1"). Same expression, different default ordering convention.
Wolfram's ToString uses OutputForm, a 2-D text layout; ours writes InputForm on one line, and names the constant ExponentialE.
Wolfram's ToString writes its own function names (Cos[x]); ours writes InputForm (Cos(x)).
